==English== ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:af|in-|consistent|text=+|tree=1}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ˌɪnkənˈsɪstənt/}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Naomi Persephone Amethyst (NaomiAmethyst)-inconsistent.wav|a=GA}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vininn126-inconsistent.wav|a=US}} ===Adjective=== {{en-adj}} # Not [[consistent]]: #: {{ant|en|consistent}} ## {{senseid|en|incompatible}}Not [[compatible]] (with another thing); [[incompatible]], [[discrepant]], [[at odds]]. ##: {{ux|en|His account of the evening was '''inconsistent''' with the security-camera footage.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1978|last=Kołakowski|first=Leszek|authorlink=Leszek Kołakowski|title=w:Main Currents of Marxism|volume=II: The Golden Age|origlang=pl|original=Główne nurty marksizmu: rozwój|translator=P[aul] S[teven] Falla|origyear=1976|publisher=w:Clarendon Press|location=w:Oxford|isbn=9780198245698|oclc=961252281|page=464|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/maincurrentsofma00lesz/page/464|passage=There was of course no question of admitting that the two texts were in any way '''inconsistent''' with each other.}} ## [[lack|Lacking]] [[internal]] [[consistency]]; self-[[contradict]]ing; not compatible with itself. ##: {{syn|en|spotty|mixed|streaky}} ##: {{ux|en|He gave an '''inconsistent''' account of the evening, saying he called her before eight, but later that he had not talked to her until after nine.}} ##* {{quote-book|en|year=1862|editor=Robert Aspland|title=The Christian Reformer |passage=He was one of those men of '''inconsistent''' politics, governed at once by prejudice and sympathies, whose 'attitude' it is impossible to foretell.}} ## Not consistent or coherent in thought or behavior. ##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1848|journal=The Columbian Magazine|volume=9|page=88 |passage=“Take him for better or worse,” added Mr. Lee, “and I think he is the strangest and most '''inconsistent''' man I ever saw.”
“'''Inconsistent'''!” resumed Mr. Jones. “He is worse than '''inconsistent'''. Inconsistencies may be pardoned as constitutional defects [...]”}} ## {{lb|en|logic}} Having the property that a [[contradiction]] can be derived. ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|inconsistentness |inconsistently}} ====Related terms==== * {{l|en|inconsistency}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top|not [[compatible]]}} * Bulgarian: * German: * Hungarian: * Latin: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|not consistent}} * Arabic: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Latin: * Māori: * Norwegian: * Occitan: * Plautdietsch: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|рассогласованный}}, {{t+|ru|непостоя́нный}}, {{t+|ru|непосле́довательный}}, {{t+|ru|противоречи́вый}}, {{t+|ru|неусто́йчивый}}, {{t+|ru|изме́нчивый}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=ceiinnnosstt|nonscientist}}
